decisions.choice: and these are the names: the words that open Genesis 46:8, and the Hebrew name of the book
decisions.reason: The book begins with "and", tying it to Genesis: the list repeats Genesis 46:8-27 and picks up the story where Genesis 50 left it. Jewish tradition names the book from these opening words ("Names"); "Exodus" ("going out") is the Septuagint's title.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel: here Jacob's twelve sons, who are named in verses 2-5
decisions.reason: The same phrase means the whole people of Israel from verse 7 on. Here, before the people has grown, it still means the sons of the man Jacob, whose other name was Israel (Genesis 32:28).

decisions.choice: each and his household: each son came with his own family
decisions.reason: "House" here is a household: a man's wife, children and others who lived under him.

decisions.choice: Jacob, who was also called Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says that Jacob and Israel are one man, which a new reader would not know, and puts the journey before the list.

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("vinrent", "arrivèrent"); passé composé at Readable ("est allé"); speech in the tenses of speech at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Exodus, as the French style guide sets for narrative: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé the tense of spoken French and of the plain Readable level. The laws and instructions of chapters 20-40 use the future or present at Literal and Balanced, as the Pentateuch terms list sets.

records.literal_gloss: And was all [the] persons coming out of [the] thigh of Jacob seventy persons, and Joseph was in Egypt.

en.L: And all the persons who came out of the thigh of Jacob were seventy persons; and Joseph was [already] in Egypt.
en.B: Seventy people in all were descended from Jacob. Joseph himself was already in Egypt.
en.R: Jacob's family had seventy people in it, counting his children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren. Joseph was already living in Egypt.

es.L: Y todas las personas que salieron del muslo de Jacob eran setenta personas; y José estaba [ya] en Egipto.
es.B: Los descendientes de Jacob eran setenta personas en total. José ya estaba en Egipto.
es.R: La familia de Jacob tenía setenta personas, contando a sus hijos, sus nietos y sus bisnietos. José ya vivía en Egipto.

fr.L: Et toutes les personnes sorties de la cuisse de Jacob étaient soixante-dix personnes ; et Joseph était [déjà] en Égypte.
fr.B: Les descendants de Jacob étaient au nombre de soixante-dix en tout. Joseph, lui, se trouvait déjà en Égypte.
fr.R: La famille de Jacob comptait soixante-dix personnes, avec ses enfants, ses petits-enfants et ses arrière-petits-enfants. Joseph vivait déjà en Égypte.

sw.L: Na nafsi zote zilizotoka katika paja la Yakobo zilikuwa nafsi sabini; naye Yusufu alikuwa [tayari] Misri.
sw.B: Wazao wote wa Yakobo walikuwa watu sabini. Yusufu mwenyewe alikuwa tayari yuko Misri.
sw.R: Jamaa ya Yakobo ilikuwa na watu sabini, wakiwemo watoto wake, wajukuu wake na vitukuu wake. Yusufu alikuwa tayari anaishi Misri.

decisions.choice: who came out of Jacob's thigh: Jacob's own descendants
decisions.reason: "Thigh" stands for a man's power to father children, as in Genesis 46:26. The count is of Jacob's offspring, not of wives or servants.

decisions.choice: seventy, as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Septuagint, and a Hebrew manuscript of Exodus from Qumran, read seventy-five. Stephen follows that number in Acts 7:14. The Septuagint reaches the same number in Genesis 46:27 by adding further descendants of Joseph. Genesis 46:27 and Deuteronomy 10:22 in the Hebrew text have seventy.

decisions.choice: counting his children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren
decisions.reason: Genesis 46:8-27 lists sons, grandsons and two great-grandsons. Readable says so, since "family" alone could suggest wives and servants as well.

records.literal_gloss: And died Joseph and all his brothers and all that generation.

en.L: And Joseph died, and all his brothers, and all that generation.
en.B: In time Joseph died, and so did all his brothers and everyone of that generation.
en.R: Later, Joseph died. All his brothers died too, and so did everyone else who lived at that time.

es.L: Y murió José, y todos sus hermanos, y toda aquella generación.
es.B: Con el tiempo murió José, y también todos sus hermanos y toda aquella generación.
es.R: Más tarde José murió. También murieron todos sus hermanos y todos los demás que vivieron en aquella época.

fr.L: Et Joseph mourut, et tous ses frères, et toute cette génération-là.
fr.B: Avec le temps, Joseph mourut, et de même tous ses frères et tous ceux de cette génération.
fr.R: Plus tard, Joseph est mort. Tous ses frères sont morts aussi, ainsi que tous les autres gens de cette époque.

sw.L: Naye Yusufu akafa, na ndugu zake wote, na kizazi kile chote.
sw.B: Baada ya muda Yusufu alikufa, vivyo hivyo ndugu zake wote na watu wote wa kizazi kile.
sw.R: Baadaye Yusufu alikufa. Ndugu zake wote walikufa pia, na watu wengine wote walioishi wakati huo.

decisions.choice: a closing statement: the generation that came down to Egypt has passed away
decisions.reason: The verse closes Genesis (50:26 tells of Joseph's death) and opens a gap of time. Exodus 12:40 puts the whole stay in Egypt at 430 years.

decisions.choice: In time / Later
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "and" begins a new stage in the story. Balanced and Readable say that time has passed.

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Israel were fruitful and swarmed and multiplied and grew mighty with very very [much], and was filled the land [with] them.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel were fruitful and swarmed and multiplied and became strong, very, very [much], and the land was filled with them.
en.B: But the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} were fruitful; they teemed and multiplied and grew exceedingly strong, until the land was full of them.
en.R: But the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had many, many children. Their numbers grew and grew, and they became very strong. Soon they were everywhere in the land.

es.L: Y los hijos de Israel fructificaron, y pulularon, y se multiplicaron, y se hicieron fuertes en extremo, en extremo; y la tierra se llenó de ellos.
es.B: Pero los israelitas fueron fecundos; se reprodujeron en abundancia, se multiplicaron y se hicieron extraordinariamente fuertes, hasta que el país se llenó de ellos.
es.R: Pero los israelitas tuvieron muchísimos hijos. Cada vez eran más y más, y se hicieron muy fuertes. Pronto estaban por todas partes en el país.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël furent féconds, et pullulèrent, et se multiplièrent, et devinrent très, très puissants ; et le pays fut rempli d’eux.
fr.B: Mais les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} furent féconds ; ils pullulèrent, se multiplièrent et devinrent extrêmement puissants, si bien que le pays fut rempli d’eux.
fr.R: Mais les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont eu beaucoup, beaucoup d’enfants. Ils sont devenus de plus en plus nombreux, et très forts. Bientôt, il y en avait partout dans le pays.

sw.L: Na wana wa Israeli wakazaa, wakajaa tele, wakaongezeka, wakawa hodari mno mno; nayo nchi ikajazwa nao.
sw.B: Lakini Waisraeli walizaa sana; waliongezeka kwa wingi mno, wakazidi kuwa na nguvu nyingi, hata wakaijaza nchi.
sw.R: Lakini Waisraeli walizaa watoto wengi sana. Idadi yao iliendelea kuongezeka, wakawa na nguvu sana. Muda si mrefu walikuwa kila mahali nchini.

decisions.choice: were fruitful ... swarmed ... multiplied ... filled: the words of the blessing in Genesis
decisions.reason: The verbs are those of Genesis 1:20-28 and 9:1, 7 ("be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth"), and of God's promise to Abraham and Jacob (Genesis 17:2; 35:11). God's blessing on humankind is being fulfilled in Israel, even in Egypt.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel: from here on, the people descended from Jacob
decisions.reason: In verse 1 the phrase meant Jacob's sons. Now it means the whole people, men and women.

decisions.choice: swarmed: increased in great numbers, like teeming creatures
decisions.reason: The verb is used of fish and small creatures that fill the waters and the ground (Genesis 1:20-21; 8:17). It is a picture of great numbers, not an insult.

decisions.choice: the land: the land of Egypt where they lived, probably the region of Goshen
decisions.reason: The Israelites were settled in Goshen (Genesis 47:27). The word can mean the earth or a country; here it is the land where they lived.

decisions.choice: children of Israel / Israelites; with the traditional setting, sons of Israel
decisions.reason: The phrase now means the whole people, women as well as men, so the default is inclusive. The gender setting gives the traditional "sons of Israel".

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "and" sets the growth of the people against the deaths in verse 6. The generation died, but the people did not shrink.

decisions.choice: los hijos de Israel (L); los israelitas (B, R), with no gender span
alternatives: {{gender:los hijos e hijas|los hijos}} de Israel
decisions.reason: For the whole of Exodus and the Pentateuch. From this verse the phrase means the whole people (m2). Spanish "hijos" in the plural already takes in daughters, so Spanish has no second wording for the gender setting to offer, and "los hijos de Israel" (L) and "los israelitas" (B, R) stand without a span. In verse 1 the same "los hijos de Israel" means Jacob's twelve sons.

decisions.choice: les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël (L); les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} (B, R)
alternatives: les fils d'Israël without a setting
les enfants d'Israël at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Exodus and the Pentateuch. From this verse the phrase means the whole people, women as well as men (m2), so the default is inclusive, as in English: "les enfants d'Israël" at Literal, which keeps the Hebrew "sons" as a family word, and "les Israélites" at Balanced and Readable. The gender setting gives the traditional "les fils d'Israël". In verse 1, where the phrase means Jacob's twelve sons, French writes "les fils d'Israël" with no span.

decisions.choice: wana wa Israeli (L); Waisraeli (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: For the whole of Exodus and the Pentateuch. From this verse the phrase means the whole people (m2). Swahili "wana" (children) is not limited to sons, and "Waisraeli" names the people, so Swahili needs no gender span. In verse 1 "wana wa Israeli" means Jacob's twelve sons.

records.literal_gloss: And arose [a] new king over Egypt who did not know Joseph.

en.L: And a new king arose over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.
en.B: Then a new king came to the throne of Egypt, one who had never heard of Joseph.
en.R: Then a new king began to rule Egypt. He knew nothing about Joseph or what he had done for Egypt.

es.L: Y se levantó un rey nuevo sobre Egipto, el cual no conocía a José.
es.B: Después subió al trono de Egipto un nuevo rey, que nunca había oído hablar de José.
es.R: Luego un nuevo rey empezó a gobernar Egipto. No sabía nada de José ni de lo que José había hecho por Egipto.

fr.L: Et un roi nouveau se leva sur l’Égypte, qui ne connaissait pas Joseph.
fr.B: Puis un nouveau roi monta sur le trône d’Égypte, un roi qui n’avait jamais entendu parler de Joseph.
fr.R: Ensuite, un nouveau roi a commencé à régner sur l’Égypte. Il ne savait rien de Joseph, ni de ce que Joseph avait fait pour l’Égypte.

sw.L: Kisha akainuka mfalme mpya juu ya Misri, ambaye hakumjua Yusufu.
sw.B: Kisha mfalme mpya alitawala Misri, mfalme ambaye hakuwahi kusikia habari za Yusufu.
sw.R: Baadaye mfalme mpya alianza kutawala Misri. Hakujua lolote kuhusu Yusufu, wala mambo aliyoifanyia Misri.

decisions.choice: did not know Joseph: knew nothing of him, and so had no regard for him or his family
decisions.reason: "Know" in Hebrew includes recognising and caring about. The new king either did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt, or chose to ignore it. Either way, Joseph's family no longer had protection at court.

decisions.choice: a new king: the king is not named
decisions.reason: Exodus never gives the name of the pharaoh. The Bible text does not settle which king of Egypt is meant.

decisions.choice: or what he had done for Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable says why it mattered that the king did not know Joseph: Joseph had saved Egypt in the famine (Genesis 41).

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֶל־עַמּ֑וֹ הִנֵּ֗ה עַ֚ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל רַ֥ב וְעָצ֖וּם מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to his people, look, [the] people of [the] sons of Israel [is] many and mighty more than us.

en.L: And he said to his people, "Look, the people of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel [are] more numerous and mightier than we.
en.B: He said to his people, "See how the people of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} have become too many and too strong for us.
en.R: He told his people, "Look! There are too many {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and they are stronger than we are.

es.L: Y dijo a su pueblo: «{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, el pueblo de los hijos de Israel [es] más numeroso y más fuerte que nosotros.
es.B: Dijo a su pueblo: «{{plural_you:Vean|Ved}} cómo el pueblo de los israelitas se ha vuelto demasiado numeroso y demasiado fuerte para nosotros.
es.R: Le dijo a su pueblo: «¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}! Hay demasiados israelitas, y son más fuertes que nosotros.

fr.L: Et il dit à son peuple : « Voici, le peuple des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël [est] plus nombreux et plus puissant que nous.
fr.B: Il dit à son peuple : « Voyez comme le peuple des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} est devenu trop nombreux et trop fort pour nous.
fr.R: Il a dit à son peuple : « Regardez ! Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} sont trop nombreux, et ils sont plus forts que nous.

sw.L: Naye akawaambia watu wake, "Tazameni, watu wa wana wa Israeli [ni] wengi na wenye nguvu kuliko sisi.
sw.B: Akawaambia watu wake, "Angalieni jinsi taifa la Waisraeli lilivyokuwa kubwa mno na lenye nguvu kutuzidi.
sw.R: Aliwaambia watu wake, "Angalieni! Waisraeli ni wengi mno, nao wana nguvu kuliko sisi.

decisions.choice: many and mighty more than us: either more numerous than the Egyptians, or too numerous for the Egyptians to control
alternatives: more numerous and stronger than we are
decisions.reason: The Hebrew comparison can mean either. It is unlikely that the Israelites outnumbered the whole of Egypt, so the king may be saying that they are too strong for Egypt to feel safe. In either case the king speaks from fear.

decisions.choice: the people of the sons of Israel: for the first time in the Bible, Israel is called a people
decisions.reason: The family of seventy has become a nation. The king's words fulfil God's promise to make Jacob a great nation in Egypt (Genesis 46:3).

source.text: הָ֥בָה נִֽתְחַכְּמָ֖ה ל֑וֹ פֶּן־יִרְבֶּ֗ה וְהָיָ֞ה כִּֽי־תִקְרֶ֤אנָה מִלְחָמָה֙ וְנוֹסַ֤ף גַּם־הוּא֙ עַל־שֹׂ֣נְאֵ֔ינוּ וְנִלְחַם־בָּ֖נוּ וְעָלָ֥ה מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Come, let us deal wisely with it, lest it multiply, and it will be when happens war, and it also will be added to [those] hating us and fight against us and go up from the land.

en.L: Come, let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply, and it happen that when war occurs, they also join those who hate us and fight against us and go up from the land."
en.B: Come, we must outwit them, or they will grow even more numerous. Then, if there is a war, they could side with our enemies, fight us, and escape from the land."
en.R: We must find a clever way to deal with them. If we do not, there will be even more of them. Then, if a war starts, they might join our enemies and fight against us. Then they would leave our country."

es.L: Vamos, obremos con astucia con ellos, no sea que se multipliquen y suceda que, cuando sobrevenga una guerra, también ellos se unan a los que nos odian, y peleen contra nosotros, y suban de la tierra».
es.B: Vamos, tenemos que ser más listos que ellos, o se harán aún más numerosos. Y si hay una guerra, podrían ponerse del lado de nuestros enemigos, luchar contra nosotros y escaparse del país».
es.R: Tenemos que encontrar una manera astuta de tratarlos. Si no lo hacemos, habrá todavía más de ellos. Y si empieza una guerra, podrían unirse a nuestros enemigos y pelear contra nosotros. Después se irían de nuestro país».

fr.L: Allons, agissons habilement envers eux, de peur qu’ils ne se multiplient, et qu’il n’arrive, quand surviendra une guerre, qu’eux aussi se joignent à ceux qui nous haïssent, et combattent contre nous, et montent hors du pays. »
fr.B: Allons, il faut ruser avec eux, sinon ils deviendront plus nombreux encore. Et s’il y a une guerre, ils pourraient se ranger du côté de nos ennemis, nous combattre et s’enfuir du pays. »
fr.R: Il faut trouver un moyen habile de les tenir. Sinon, ils seront encore plus nombreux. Et si une guerre commence, ils risquent de se joindre à nos ennemis et de se battre contre nous. Ensuite, ils quitteraient notre pays. »

sw.L: Haya, na tuwatendee kwa hekima, wasije wakaongezeka, na ikawa vita vitakapotokea, wao nao wakajiunga na wale wanaotuchukia, wakapigana nasi, wakapanda kutoka katika nchi hii."
sw.B: Haya, lazima tuwazidi kwa werevu, la sivyo wataongezeka zaidi. Kisha vita vikitokea, wanaweza kujiunga na adui zetu, wakapigana nasi, wakatoroka kutoka nchi hii."
sw.R: Lazima tutafute njia ya ujanja ya kuwashughulikia. Tusipofanya hivyo, wataongezeka zaidi. Tena vita vikianza, wanaweza kujiunga na adui zetu na kupigana nasi. Kisha wataondoka katika nchi yetu."

decisions.choice: let us deal wisely: let us be shrewd, find a clever plan
decisions.reason: The verb is from the word for wisdom. Here it is cunning that serves cruelty. The irony runs through the chapter: the king's plans keep failing (verses 12, 17, 20).

decisions.choice: with it ... it multiply: the people as one body, "it"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the people with a singular pronoun, as one body. The sense is plural: the Israelites.

decisions.choice: go up from the land: leave the country
alternatives: gain the upper hand in the land
decisions.reason: "Go up" from Egypt is the usual phrase for leaving it for Canaan (Genesis 13:1; 50:24). The king's fear is that he will lose his labor force. Some read the phrase as "gain control of the land", but the usual sense is to leave it.

decisions.choice: when war happens: the verb is feminine plural in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The verb form does not agree with "war". It may be an old form of the singular; the Samaritan Pentateuch and the Septuagint read it as "befalls us". The meaning is the same: if a war comes.

decisions.choice: them, they
decisions.reason: English uses the plural for the people, as the Hebrew uses a singular "it".

source.text: וַיָּשִׂ֤ימוּ עָלָיו֙ שָׂרֵ֣י מִסִּ֔ים לְמַ֥עַן עַנֹּת֖וֹ בְּסִבְלֹתָ֑ם וַיִּ֜בֶן עָרֵ֤י מִסְכְּנוֹת֙ לְפַרְעֹ֔ה אֶת־פִּתֹ֖ם וְאֶת־רַעַמְסֵֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set over it officers of forced labor so as to afflict it with their burdens, and it built store cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Rameses.

en.L: And they set over them officers of forced labor, in order to afflict them with their burdens; and they built cities of storage for Pharaoh: Pithom and Rameses.
en.B: So the Egyptians put taskmasters over them to crush them with heavy loads, and the Israelites built supply cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Rameses.
en.R: So the Egyptians put men in charge of the Israelites to force them to work hard. They made the Israelites carry heavy loads. The Israelites built two cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Rameses, where supplies could be stored.

es.L: Y pusieron sobre ellos jefes de trabajos forzados para afligirlos con sus cargas; y edificaron ciudades de almacenamiento para el faraón: Pitón y Ramsés.
es.B: Así que los egipcios pusieron capataces sobre ellos para oprimirlos con cargas pesadas, y los israelitas construyeron para el faraón las ciudades de almacenes de Pitón y Ramsés.
es.R: Entonces los egipcios pusieron hombres al mando de los israelitas para obligarlos a trabajar duro. Les hacían llevar cargas pesadas. Los israelitas construyeron dos ciudades para el faraón, Pitón y Ramsés, donde se podían guardar provisiones.

fr.L: Et ils établirent sur eux des chefs de corvée, afin de les opprimer par leurs fardeaux ; et ils bâtirent des villes d’entrepôts pour Pharaon : Pithom et Ramsès.
fr.B: Les Égyptiens placèrent donc sur eux des chefs de corvée pour les accabler de lourdes charges, et les Israélites bâtirent pour Pharaon les villes d’entrepôts de Pithom et de Ramsès.
fr.R: Alors les Égyptiens ont mis des chefs à la tête des Israélites pour les obliger à travailler dur. Ils leur faisaient porter de lourdes charges. Les Israélites ont construit deux villes pour Pharaon, Pithom et Ramsès, où l’on pouvait garder des provisions.

sw.L: Nao wakaweka juu yao wakuu wa kazi za kulazimishwa, ili wawatese kwa mizigo yao; nao wakamjengea Farao miji ya ghala: Pithomu na Ramesesi.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo Wamisri waliweka wasimamizi juu yao ili wawakandamize kwa mizigo mizito, nao Waisraeli wakamjengea Farao miji ya kuhifadhia akiba, Pithomu na Ramesesi.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Wamisri waliweka watu wa kuwasimamia Waisraeli ili wawalazimishe kufanya kazi ngumu. Waliwafanya Waisraeli kubeba mizigo mizito. Waisraeli walimjengea Farao miji miwili, Pithomu na Ramesesi, ambamo akiba ya chakula iliweza kuhifadhiwa.

decisions.choice: officers of forced labor: men in charge of work gangs
decisions.reason: The second word is the term for forced, unpaid labor owed to a king, as under Solomon (1 Kings 5:13-14; 9:15-21). The Israelites became a work force for the state.

decisions.choice: to afflict: to oppress, to wear down
decisions.reason: This is the verb of God's word to Abraham, that his descendants would be afflicted in a foreign land for four hundred years (Genesis 15:13).

decisions.choice: store cities Pithom and Rameses: cities in the eastern Nile delta where supplies were kept
decisions.reason: "Rameses" is the name of the region in Genesis 47:11 and of a city in the eastern delta. "Pharaoh" is the Egyptian title for the king, not a personal name.

decisions.choice: the Egyptians ... the Israelites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "they" and "it". Balanced and Readable name who is meant.

decisions.choice: el faraón
decisions.reason: For the whole of Exodus, as in Genesis: Spanish treats the Egyptian title as a common noun with the article (m3), "el faraón", where the English writes "Pharaoh" without one.

decisions.choice: Pharaon, without an article, where the English says "Pharaoh"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Exodus, as in Genesis: the English uses "Pharaoh" as if it were a name, and French does the same with "Pharaon" without an article, the long-standing French usage. "Le pharaon" (the title, m3) is kept for the few places where the English says "the pharaoh".

source.text: וְכַאֲשֶׁר֙ יְעַנּ֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ כֵּ֥ן יִרְבֶּ֖ה וְכֵ֣ן יִפְרֹ֑ץ וַיָּקֻ֕צוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And just as they afflicted it, so it multiplied and so it spread, and they dreaded because of [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and the more they spread out; and they came to dread the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: Yet the harder they were oppressed, the more they increased and spread out, until the Egyptians came to loathe and fear the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.
en.R: But the more the Egyptians made the Israelites suffer, the more children they had, and the more they spread through the land. So the Egyptians became afraid of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

es.L: Y cuanto más los afligían, tanto más se multiplicaban y tanto más se extendían; y llegaron a sentir pavor de los hijos de Israel.
es.B: Pero cuanto más los oprimían, más crecían y más se extendían, hasta que los egipcios llegaron a sentir asco y miedo de los israelitas.
es.R: Pero cuanto más hacían sufrir los egipcios a los israelitas, más hijos tenían estos, y más se extendían por el país. Por eso los egipcios empezaron a tener miedo de los israelitas.

fr.L: Et plus ils les opprimaient, plus ils se multipliaient et plus ils se répandaient ; et l’on se mit à redouter les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël.
fr.B: Pourtant, plus on les opprimait, plus ils se multipliaient et se répandaient, si bien que les Égyptiens en vinrent à éprouver pour les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} du dégoût et de la peur.
fr.R: Mais plus les Égyptiens faisaient souffrir les Israélites, plus ceux-ci avaient d’enfants, et plus ils se répandaient dans le pays. Alors les Égyptiens ont commencé à avoir peur des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}.

sw.L: Na kadiri walivyowatesa, ndivyo walivyoongezeka na ndivyo walivyoenea; nao wakaingiwa na hofu kwa sababu ya wana wa Israeli.
sw.B: Lakini kadiri walivyozidi kukandamizwa, ndivyo walivyozidi kuongezeka na kuenea, hata Wamisri wakawachukia Waisraeli na kuwaogopa.
sw.R: Lakini kadiri Wamisri walivyowatesa Waisraeli, ndivyo Waisraeli walivyozidi kupata watoto na kuenea katika nchi. Kwa hiyo Wamisri wakaanza kuwaogopa Waisraeli.

decisions.choice: just as ... so: the more ... the more
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the two sides side by side: as the oppression grew, so did the people. The king's plan has the opposite effect.

decisions.choice: they dreaded: a mixture of fear and disgust
decisions.reason: The verb is used of feeling sick of something (Numbers 21:5) and of being in dread of someone (Numbers 22:3). Both may be meant: the Egyptians were afraid of the Israelites and loathed them.

decisions.choice: the Egyptians
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. The context shows that the Egyptians are meant.

source.text: וַיַּעֲבִ֧דוּ מִצְרַ֛יִם אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּפָֽרֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And made labor Egypt [the] sons of Israel with harshness.

en.L: And the Egyptians made the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel serve with harshness,
en.B: The Egyptians forced the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to work without mercy,
en.R: The Egyptians made the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} work as slaves, and they were cruel to them.

es.L: Y los egipcios obligaron a los hijos de Israel a servir con crueldad,
es.B: Los egipcios obligaron a los israelitas a trabajar sin piedad,
es.R: Los egipcios hicieron trabajar a los israelitas como esclavos, y los trataban con crueldad.

fr.L: Et les Égyptiens firent servir les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël avec rigueur,
fr.B: Les Égyptiens forcèrent les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} à travailler sans pitié,
fr.R: Les Égyptiens ont obligé les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} à travailler comme des esclaves, et ils ont été cruels avec eux.

sw.L: Nao Wamisri wakawatumikisha wana wa Israeli kwa ukali,
sw.B: Wamisri waliwalazimisha Waisraeli kufanya kazi bila huruma,
sw.R: Wamisri waliwafanya Waisraeli kufanya kazi kama watumwa, wakawatendea ukatili.

decisions.choice: made [them] serve with harshness: forced them into slavery and treated them ruthlessly
decisions.reason: The verb for "serve" or "work" comes five times in verses 13-14; it is the word for service that a slave gives. The Israelites who are made to serve Pharaoh will later be freed to serve God (4:23; 7:16). The word for harshness is the one in Leviticus 25:43, 46, which forbids an Israelite to rule over a fellow Israelite in this way.

decisions.choice: Egypt: the people of Egypt, the Egyptians
decisions.reason: The name of the country stands for its people, with a plural verb.

decisions.choice: work as slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" in Readable, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt (m1).

decisions.choice: como esclavos
decisions.reason: For the whole of Exodus: "esclavo" at every level for Israel's slavery in Egypt, as the English keeps "slave" for it (r-en-1); elsewhere the word for a servant is "esclavo" at Literal and "siervo" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: comme des esclaves
decisions.reason: For the whole of Exodus: "esclave" at every level for Israel's slavery in Egypt, as the English keeps "slave" for it (r-en-1); elsewhere the word for a servant is "esclave" at Literal and "serviteur" at Balanced and Readable, as the Pentateuch terms list sets.

decisions.choice: kama watumwa
decisions.reason: For the whole of Exodus: "mtumwa" (slave) at every level for Israel's slavery in Egypt, as the English keeps "slave" for it (r-en-1); elsewhere the word for a servant is "mtumwa" at Literal and "mtumishi" at Balanced and Readable.

source.text: וַיְמָרְר֨וּ אֶת־חַיֵּיהֶ֜ם בַּעֲבֹדָ֣ה קָשָׁ֗ה בְּחֹ֨מֶר֙ וּבִלְבֵנִ֔ים וּבְכָל־עֲבֹדָ֖ה בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה אֵ֚ת כָּל־עֲבֹ֣דָתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־עָבְד֥וּ בָהֶ֖ם בְּפָֽרֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they made bitter their lives with hard labor in mortar and in bricks and in all labor in the field, all their labor which they labored [by] them with harshness.

en.L: and they made their lives bitter with hard service in mortar and in bricks and in every [kind of] service in the field: all their service in which they made them serve with harshness.
en.B: and made their lives bitter with hard labor, mixing mortar, making bricks, and doing every kind of work in the fields. In all this labor they drove them without mercy.
en.R: They made life very hard for them. The Israelites had to mix mud and make bricks, and do all kinds of hard work in the fields. The Egyptians showed them no mercy in any of this work.

es.L: y amargaron su vida con duro servicio en barro y en ladrillos y en todo [tipo de] servicio en el campo: todo su servicio en que los hacían servir con crueldad.
es.B: y les amargaron la vida con trabajos pesados, preparando barro, fabricando ladrillos y haciendo toda clase de tareas en el campo. En todos estos trabajos los trataban sin piedad.
es.R: Les hicieron la vida muy dura. Los israelitas tenían que mezclar barro y hacer ladrillos, y hacer toda clase de trabajos pesados en el campo. Los egipcios no les tuvieron ninguna compasión en ninguno de estos trabajos.

fr.L: et ils rendirent leur vie amère par un dur service, dans l’argile et dans les briques, et par toute [sorte de] service dans les champs : tout le service où ils les firent servir avec rigueur.
fr.B: et leur rendirent la vie amère par de durs travaux : préparer le mortier, faire des briques, accomplir toutes sortes de travaux dans les champs. Dans tout ce labeur, ils les menaient sans pitié.
fr.R: Ils leur ont rendu la vie très dure. Les Israélites devaient mélanger de la boue et faire des briques, et faire toutes sortes de travaux pénibles dans les champs. Dans tout ce travail, les Égyptiens ne leur ont montré aucune pitié.

sw.L: nao wakayafanya maisha yao kuwa machungu kwa utumishi mgumu katika matope na katika matofali, na katika kila [aina ya] utumishi mashambani: utumishi wao wote waliowatumikisha kwa ukali.
sw.B: na wakayafanya maisha yao kuwa machungu kwa kazi ngumu ya kukanda udongo, kufyatua matofali na kufanya kila aina ya kazi mashambani. Katika kazi hizo zote waliwatumikisha bila huruma.
sw.R: Waliyafanya maisha yao kuwa magumu sana. Waisraeli walilazimika kukanda matope na kufyatua matofali, na kufanya kila aina ya kazi ngumu mashambani. Wamisri hawakuwaonea huruma hata kidogo katika kazi hizo zote.

decisions.choice: made bitter their lives: made life hard and miserable
decisions.reason: The bitterness is remembered at Passover with bitter herbs (12:8).

decisions.choice: mortar and bricks: building with sun-dried mud brick
decisions.reason: Egypt built with bricks of mud mixed with straw (5:7-18), set in mud mortar. The word for mortar can also mean clay.

decisions.choice: all their labor which they made them serve: a summary of everything before
decisions.reason: The last clause sums up the list: in every kind of work, the Egyptians drove them hard. The verb "serve" or "labor" appears again and again, making the point by repetition.

decisions.choice: service ... serve
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the repetition of the Hebrew root, which Balanced and Readable vary for natural English.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם לַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֖ת הָֽעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת אֲשֶׁ֨ר שֵׁ֤ם הָֽאַחַת֙ שִׁפְרָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית פּוּעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] king of Egypt to the Hebrew midwives, of whom [the] name of the one [was] Shiphrah and [the] name of the second [was] Puah,

en.L: And the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one [was] Shiphrah and the name of the second [was] Puah,
en.B: The king of Egypt also spoke to the Hebrew midwives, one named Shiphrah and the other Puah.
en.R: There were two women who helped the Hebrew women give birth. Their names were Shiphrah and Puah. The king of Egypt spoke to them.

es.L: Y el rey de Egipto dijo a las parteras hebreas, de las cuales el nombre de una [era] Sifrá y el nombre de la segunda [era] Fuá,
es.B: El rey de Egipto habló también a las parteras hebreas, una llamada Sifrá y la otra Fuá.
es.R: Había dos mujeres que ayudaban a las hebreas a dar a luz. Se llamaban Sifrá y Fuá. El rey de Egipto habló con ellas.

fr.L: Et le roi d’Égypte dit aux sages-femmes hébreues, dont le nom de l’une [était] Shiphra et le nom de la seconde [était] Poua,
fr.B: Le roi d’Égypte parla aussi aux sages-femmes hébreues, l’une nommée Shiphra et l’autre Poua.
fr.R: Il y avait deux femmes qui aidaient les femmes hébreues à accoucher. Elles s’appelaient Shiphra et Poua. Le roi d’Égypte leur a parlé.

sw.L: Naye mfalme wa Misri akawaambia wakunga Waebrania, ambao jina la mmoja [lilikuwa] Shifra na jina la wa pili [lilikuwa] Pua,
sw.B: Mfalme wa Misri aliwaambia pia wakunga Waebrania, mmoja aitwaye Shifra na mwingine Pua.
sw.R: Kulikuwa na wanawake wawili waliowasaidia wanawake wa Kiebrania kujifungua. Majina yao yalikuwa Shifra na Pua. Mfalme wa Misri aliongea nao.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew midwives: midwives who were Hebrews
alternatives: the midwives of the Hebrew women
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can also be read "the midwives of the Hebrews", that is, Egyptian women who served the Hebrews. Their names are Semitic, and they fear God (verse 17), so most likely they were Hebrews themselves. Two midwives could hardly serve a whole people; they may have been the chief midwives over others.

decisions.choice: Shiphrah and Puah: the midwives are named, the king is not
decisions.reason: The story names the two women who feared God and leaves the powerful king of Egypt nameless.

decisions.choice: Hebrew: a name for Israelites, used most of all by or to foreigners
decisions.reason: "Hebrew" is first used of Abram (Genesis 14:13). In Exodus it is the name Egyptians use for the Israelites, and the name Israelites use of themselves when speaking to Egyptians (3:18; 5:3).

decisions.choice: also
decisions.reason: The king's second plan follows the first; Balanced marks the step with "also". Balanced and Readable end the verse with a full stop, since what the king said follows in verse 16.

decisions.choice: les sages-femmes hébreues; les femmes hébreues (verses 16, 19)
decisions.reason: The midwives were most likely Hebrews themselves (m1). French has no settled feminine for "hébreu" used of persons: "hébraïque" is used of the language and of things, and "les sages-femmes des Hébreux" leans towards the other reading, Egyptian midwives who served the Hebrews. The feminine "hébreue" says plainly that they were Hebrew women; a reviewer may prefer another form.

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בְּיַלֶּדְכֶן֙ אֶת־הָֽעִבְרִיּ֔וֹת וּרְאִיתֶ֖ן עַל־הָאָבְנָ֑יִם אִם־בֵּ֥ן הוּא֙ וַהֲמִתֶּ֣ן אֹת֔וֹ וְאִם־בַּ֥ת הִ֖יא וָחָֽיָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, when you deliver the Hebrew [women], and you look on the two stones, if [it is] a son, and you shall kill him, and if [it is] a daughter, and she shall live.

en.L: and he said, "When you help the Hebrew women give birth and you look upon the birthstool, if it [is] a son, you shall kill him; but if it [is] a daughter, she shall live."
en.B: He said, "When you attend the Hebrew women in childbirth, watch as they kneel on the birthstones. If it is a son, put him to death; if a daughter, she may live."
en.R: He said to them, "When you help Hebrew women have their babies, watch as each baby is born. If it is a boy, kill him. If it is a girl, let her live."

es.L: y dijo: «Cuando {{plural_you:asistan|asistáis}} a las hebreas en el parto y {{plural_you:miren|miréis}} sobre la silla de parto, si es hijo, lo {{plural_you:matarán|mataréis}}; pero si es hija, vivirá».
es.B: Les dijo: «Cuando {{plural_you:atiendan|atendáis}} a las mujeres hebreas en el parto, {{plural_you:observen|observad}} cuando se arrodillen sobre las piedras de parto. Si es un niño, {{plural_you:mátenlo|matadlo}}; si es una niña, que viva».
es.R: Les dijo: «Cuando {{plural_you:ayuden|ayudéis}} a las mujeres hebreas a tener a sus bebés, {{plural_you:miren|mirad}} bien cuando nazca cada uno. Si es un niño, {{plural_you:mátenlo|matadlo}}. Si es una niña, {{plural_you:déjenla|dejadla}} vivir».

fr.L: et il dit : « Quand vous ferez accoucher les femmes hébreues et que vous regarderez sur le siège d’accouchement, si c’est un fils, vous le ferez mourir ; mais si c’est une fille, elle vivra. »
fr.B: Il dit : « Quand vous assisterez les femmes hébreues pendant l’accouchement, observez-les lorsqu’elles s’agenouillent sur les pierres. Si c’est un garçon, faites-le mourir ; si c’est une fille, qu’elle vive. »
fr.R: Il leur a dit : « Quand vous aidez les femmes hébreues à mettre leurs bébés au monde, regardez bien chaque bébé au moment où il naît. Si c’est un garçon, tuez-le. Si c’est une fille, laissez-la vivre. »

sw.L: naye akasema, "Mtakapowazalisha wanawake wa Kiebrania na kutazama juu ya kiti cha kuzalia, ikiwa [ni] mwana wa kiume, mtamwua; lakini ikiwa [ni] binti, ataishi."
sw.B: Alisema, "Mnapowasaidia wanawake wa Kiebrania kujifungua, waangalieni wanapopiga magoti juu ya mawe ya kuzalia. Akiwa mtoto wa kiume, mwueni; akiwa wa kike, mwacheni aishi."
sw.R: Aliwaambia, "Mnapowasaidia wanawake wa Kiebrania kuzaa, mtazameni kila mtoto anapozaliwa. Akiwa mvulana, mwueni. Akiwa msichana, mwacheni aishi."

decisions.choice: the two stones: probably the stones or stool a woman knelt or sat on to give birth
decisions.reason: The word means "the pair of stones". Egyptian women gave birth kneeling or squatting on bricks or stones. Some take the word to mean the newborn's genitals, which the midwife would look at to see whether it was a boy. Jeremiah 18:3 uses the same word for a potter's wheel. The meaning is uncertain, but the point is clear: at the moment of birth.

decisions.choice: if it is a son ... if it is a daughter
decisions.reason: "Son" and "daughter" here mean a male or a female baby.

decisions.choice: watch as each baby is born
decisions.reason: Readable gives the point of the phrase (at the moment of birth) without naming the uncertain object.

decisions.choice: ustedes forms by default (asistan, miren, matarán); vosotros forms with the plural-you setting (asistáis, miréis, mataréis)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Exodus, as in Genesis 1:22: whenever several people are addressed, Spanish must choose a plural form of address. The default is the "ustedes" form used by most Spanish speakers; the plural-you setting gives the "vosotros" form of Spain (here "vosotras" forms, the verbs being the same). The span covers each verb or pronoun that changes. French "vous" and Swahili "ninyi" need no setting.

source.text: וַתִּירֶ֤אןָ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹת֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְלֹ֣א עָשׂ֔וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ן מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרָ֑יִם וַתְּחַיֶּ֖יןָ אֶת־הַיְלָדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And feared the midwives God, and they did not do as spoke to them [the] king of Egypt, and they let live the boys.

en.L: But the midwives feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt had spoken to them, and they let the boys live.
en.B: But the midwives feared God. They did not obey the king of Egypt's order; they kept the boys alive.
en.R: But the midwives respected God and were afraid to do wrong. So they did not do what the king of Egypt told them. They let the baby boys live.

es.L: Pero las parteras temieron a Dios y no hicieron como les había hablado el rey de Egipto, sino que dejaron vivir a los niños.
es.B: Pero las parteras temían a Dios. No obedecieron la orden del rey de Egipto, sino que mantuvieron con vida a los niños.
es.R: Pero las parteras respetaban a Dios y tenían miedo de hacer el mal. Por eso no hicieron lo que el rey de Egipto les había dicho. Dejaron vivir a los niños varones.

fr.L: Mais les sages-femmes craignirent Dieu et ne firent pas comme le roi d’Égypte leur avait parlé, et elles laissèrent vivre les garçons.
fr.B: Mais les sages-femmes craignaient Dieu. Elles n’obéirent pas à l’ordre du roi d’Égypte ; elles gardèrent les garçons en vie.
fr.R: Mais les sages-femmes respectaient Dieu et avaient peur de mal agir. Alors elles n’ont pas fait ce que le roi d’Égypte leur avait dit. Elles ont laissé vivre les petits garçons.

sw.L: Lakini wakunga wakamcha Mungu, wala hawakufanya kama mfalme wa Misri alivyowaambia, bali wakawaacha hai watoto wa kiume.
sw.B: Lakini wakunga walimcha Mungu. Hawakutii agizo la mfalme wa Misri, bali waliwahifadhi hai watoto wa kiume.
sw.R: Lakini wakunga walimheshimu Mungu na waliogopa kufanya mabaya. Kwa hiyo hawakufanya kile ambacho mfalme wa Misri aliwaambia. Waliwaacha watoto wa kiume waishi.

decisions.choice: feared God: had reverence for God, and so would not do evil
decisions.reason: To fear God is to hold God in awe and to obey him, especially in how one treats the weak (Genesis 20:11; 42:18; Leviticus 19:14). The midwives' fear of God outweighs their fear of the king.

decisions.choice: let live the boys: kept the boys alive
decisions.reason: The verb means to keep alive, to preserve life. The midwives did more than leave the boys alone; they protected them.

decisions.choice: respected God and were afraid to do wrong
decisions.reason: "Fear God" can sound like terror to a new reader. Readable says what it means here: reverence that leads to doing right.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֤א מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֔ת וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ן מַדּ֥וּעַ עֲשִׂיתֶ֖ן הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַתְּחַיֶּ֖יןָ אֶת־הַיְלָדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And called [the] king of Egypt the midwives and said to them, why have you done this thing and let live the boys?

en.L: And the king of Egypt called the midwives and said to them, "Why have you done this thing and let the boys live?"
en.B: So the king of Egypt sent for the midwives and demanded, "Why have you acted like this, keeping the boys alive?"
en.R: So the king of Egypt sent for the midwives. He asked them, "Why did you do this? Why did you let the baby boys live?"

es.L: Y el rey de Egipto llamó a las parteras y les dijo: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:han hecho|habéis hecho}} esto y {{plural_you:han dejado|habéis dejado}} vivir a los niños?».
es.B: Entonces el rey de Egipto mandó llamar a las parteras y les exigió: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:se han portado|os habéis portado}} así, dejando con vida a los niños?».
es.R: Entonces el rey de Egipto mandó llamar a las parteras. Les preguntó: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} esto? ¿Por qué {{plural_you:dejaron|dejasteis}} vivir a los niños?».

fr.L: Et le roi d’Égypte appela les sages-femmes et leur dit : « Pourquoi avez-vous fait cette chose et laissé vivre les garçons ? »
fr.B: Alors le roi d’Égypte fit venir les sages-femmes et leur demanda : « Pourquoi avez-vous agi ainsi, en gardant les garçons en vie ? »
fr.R: Alors le roi d’Égypte a fait venir les sages-femmes. Il leur a demandé : « Pourquoi avez-vous fait ça ? Pourquoi avez-vous laissé vivre les petits garçons ? »

sw.L: Naye mfalme wa Misri akawaita wakunga, akawaambia, "Kwa nini mmefanya jambo hili, mkawaacha hai watoto wa kiume?"
sw.B: Basi mfalme wa Misri akawaita wakunga, akawauliza kwa ukali, "Kwa nini mmefanya hivi, mkawaacha watoto wa kiume hai?"
sw.R: Kwa hiyo mfalme wa Misri aliwaita wakunga. Akawauliza, "Kwa nini mmefanya hivi? Kwa nini mmewaacha watoto wa kiume waishi?"

decisions.choice: two questions
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is one question in two parts; Readable splits it into two short questions, the way an angry speaker would.

source.text: וַתֹּאמַ֤רְןָ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹת֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה כִּ֣י לֹ֧א כַנָּשִׁ֛ים הַמִּצְרִיֹּ֖ת הָֽעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת כִּֽי־חָי֣וֹת הֵ֔נָּה בְּטֶ֨רֶם תָּב֧וֹא אֲלֵהֶ֛ן הַמְיַלֶּ֖דֶת וְיָלָֽדוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the midwives to Pharaoh, because not like the Egyptian women [are] the Hebrew [women], for lively [are] they; before comes to them the midwife, and they have given birth.

en.L: And the midwives said to Pharaoh, "Because the Hebrew women [are] not like the Egyptian women, for they [are] lively; before the midwife comes to them, they have given birth."
en.B: The midwives told Pharaoh, "Hebrew women are different from Egyptian women. They are strong and quick, and they have their babies before the midwife gets there."
en.R: The midwives said to Pharaoh, "Hebrew women are not like Egyptian women. They are strong and healthy. Their babies are born before we can get to them."

es.L: Y las parteras dijeron al faraón: «Porque las hebreas no [son] como las mujeres egipcias, pues ellas [son] vigorosas; antes que la partera llegue a ellas, ya han dado a luz».
es.B: Las parteras le dijeron al faraón: «Las mujeres hebreas no son como las egipcias. Son fuertes y rápidas, y dan a luz antes de que llegue la partera».
es.R: Las parteras le respondieron al faraón: «Las mujeres hebreas no son como las egipcias. Son fuertes y sanas. Sus bebés nacen antes de que podamos llegar».

fr.L: Et les sages-femmes dirent à Pharaon : « C’est que les femmes hébreues ne [sont] pas comme les femmes égyptiennes, car elles [sont] vigoureuses ; avant que la sage-femme arrive auprès d’elles, elles ont accouché. »
fr.B: Les sages-femmes répondirent à Pharaon : « Les femmes hébreues ne sont pas comme les Égyptiennes. Elles sont robustes et rapides, et elles mettent leur enfant au monde avant que la sage-femme arrive. »
fr.R: Les sages-femmes ont répondu à Pharaon : « Les femmes hébreues ne sont pas comme les Égyptiennes. Elles sont fortes et en bonne santé. Leurs bébés naissent avant que nous ayons le temps d’arriver. »

sw.L: Nao wakunga wakamwambia Farao, "Kwa sababu wanawake wa Kiebrania [si] kama wanawake wa Kimisri, kwa kuwa wao [ni] wenye nguvu; kabla mkunga hajawafikia, wamekwisha kuzaa."
sw.B: Wakunga walimwambia Farao, "Wanawake wa Kiebrania si kama wanawake wa Kimisri. Wana nguvu na ni wepesi, nao hujifungua kabla mkunga hajafika."
sw.R: Wakunga walimjibu Farao, "Wanawake wa Kiebrania si kama wanawake wa Misri. Wana nguvu na afya nzuri. Watoto wao huzaliwa kabla sisi hatujafika."

decisions.choice: lively: vigorous, full of life
decisions.reason: The word comes from the root "live", the same root as the king's order (verse 16) and the midwives' deed (verse 17). The Hebrew women are full of life. A similar word means "animals", and some read the midwives as saying, with a hint of scorn, that the Hebrew women give birth like animals.

decisions.choice: the midwives' answer: a clever reply to the king
decisions.reason: The text does not say whether the answer was true. It shows the midwives outwitting the king who wanted to outwit Israel (verse 10). God blesses them for fearing him (verses 20-21).

decisions.choice: before we can get to them
decisions.reason: The midwives speak of "the midwife" in the singular, meaning any of them. Readable has them speak of themselves.

source.text: וַיֵּ֥יטֶב אֱלֹהִ֖ים לַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֑ת וַיִּ֧רֶב הָעָ֛ם וַיַּֽעַצְמ֖וּ מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And did good God to the midwives, and multiplied the people and grew mighty very.

en.L: And God did good to the midwives, and the people multiplied and became very mighty.
en.B: So God was good to the midwives, and the people kept growing in number and became very strong.
en.R: God was good to the midwives. And the Israelites kept on growing in number and became very strong.

es.L: Y Dios trató bien a las parteras; y el pueblo se multiplicó y llegó a ser muy fuerte.
es.B: Así que Dios fue bondadoso con las parteras, y el pueblo siguió creciendo en número y se hizo muy fuerte.
es.R: Dios fue bueno con las parteras. Y los israelitas siguieron aumentando en número y se hicieron muy fuertes.

fr.L: Et Dieu fut bon envers les sages-femmes ; et le peuple se multiplia et devint très puissant.
fr.B: Dieu se montra donc bienveillant envers les sages-femmes, et le peuple continua de croître et devint très fort.
fr.R: Dieu a été bon pour les sages-femmes. Et les Israélites sont devenus toujours plus nombreux et très forts.

sw.L: Naye Mungu akawatendea mema wakunga; nao watu wakaongezeka, wakawa na nguvu nyingi sana.
sw.B: Basi Mungu aliwafadhili wakunga, nao watu wakazidi kuongezeka na kuwa na nguvu sana.
sw.R: Mungu aliwatendea wakunga mema. Waisraeli nao waliendelea kuongezeka, wakawa na nguvu sana.

decisions.choice: multiplied and became mighty: the words of verse 7 again
decisions.reason: The second of the king's plans has failed too. The same verbs as verse 7 show the people still growing.

decisions.choice: the Israelites
decisions.reason: "The people" is Israel. Readable names it.

source.text: וַיְהִ֕י כִּֽי־יָֽרְא֥וּ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֖ת אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָהֶ֖ם בָּתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, because feared the midwives God, and he made for them households.

en.L: And it came about, because the midwives feared God, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made households for them.
en.B: And because the midwives feared God, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} provided them with households of their own.
en.R: Because the midwives respected God, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} blessed them with children and families.

es.L: Y sucedió que, como las parteras temieron a Dios, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les hizo familias.
es.B: Y como las parteras temían a Dios, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les concedió tener familia propia.
es.R: Como las parteras respetaban a Dios, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} las bendijo con hijos y familias.

fr.L: Et il arriva, parce que les sages-femmes avaient craint Dieu, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur fonda des familles.
fr.B: Et parce que les sages-femmes craignaient Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur donna d’avoir leur propre famille.
fr.R: Comme les sages-femmes respectaient Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a bénies en leur donnant des enfants et une famille.

sw.L: Ikawa, kwa sababu wakunga walimcha Mungu, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} akawafanyia nyumba.
sw.B: Na kwa sababu wakunga walimcha Mungu, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} akawapa jamaa zao wenyewe.
sw.R: Kwa kuwa wakunga walimheshimu Mungu, aliwabariki kwa kuwapa watoto na jamaa.

decisions.choice: made them houses: gave them families of their own
alternatives: established them as households in Israel
decisions.reason: To "make a house" for someone is to give them descendants (2 Samuel 7:11, 27; 1 Samuel 2:35). The women who kept other mothers' children alive are given children themselves.

decisions.choice: for them: the midwives
decisions.reason: The pronoun is masculine, which Hebrew sometimes uses for women. A few take it to mean the Israelites; the context points to the midwives.

decisions.choice: blessed them with children and families
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "made houses for them" means.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}
decisions.reason: For the whole of Exodus, as in Genesis: the deity pronoun setting goes on the Spanish words for God that Spanish writes out (él, lo, le, su, mí, me, tú, te, ti, tu); where Spanish has no separate word for the English pronoun, there is no span. Here the subject changes from the midwives to God, so Spanish writes the pronoun "él" to make clear who acted, and it takes the span.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}
decisions.reason: For the whole of Exodus, as in Genesis: every pronoun for God takes the deity pronoun setting, lowercase by default and capitalised as the alternative (il, lui, le, l', son, sa, ses, and moi, me, mon, toi, te, tu, ton when God speaks or is spoken to, including an inverted "-tu"). "Je" has no span, and a pronoun that opens a sentence is written plainly with its capital.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} akawafanyia (L, B); no span at Readable (aliwabariki)
alternatives: no span, with the subject only in the verb
decisions.reason: For the whole of Exodus, as in Genesis: Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb, where no capital is possible, so the deity pronoun setting goes only on free pronouns for God (yeye, naye, mimi, nami, wewe, and the possessives wake, yake, wangu, yako...). At Literal and Balanced the change of subject from the midwives to God is marked with a free "yeye", which takes the span; Readable leaves the subject in the verb.

source.text: וַיְצַ֣ו פַּרְעֹ֔ה לְכָל־עַמּ֖וֹ לֵאמֹ֑ר כָּל־הַבֵּ֣ן הַיִּלּ֗וֹד הַיְאֹ֨רָה֙ תַּשְׁלִיכֻ֔הוּ וְכָל־הַבַּ֖ת תְּחַיּֽוּן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And commanded Pharaoh all his people, saying, every son who is born to the River you shall throw him, and every daughter you shall let live.

en.L: And Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, "Every son who is born, into the River you shall throw him; and every daughter you shall let live."
en.B: Then Pharaoh gave an order to all his people: "Every boy that is born must be thrown into the Nile, but every girl is to be spared."
en.R: Then Pharaoh gave an order to all the Egyptians: "When a Hebrew baby boy is born, throw him into the Nile River. But let all the baby girls live."

es.L: Y el faraón mandó a todo su pueblo, diciendo: «Todo hijo que nazca, al Río lo {{plural_you:echarán|echaréis}}; y a toda hija la {{plural_you:dejarán|dejaréis}} vivir».
es.B: Entonces el faraón dio una orden a todo su pueblo: «Todo niño que nazca debe ser arrojado al Nilo, pero a toda niña se le perdonará la vida».
es.R: Entonces el faraón dio una orden a todos los egipcios: «Cuando nazca un niño hebreo, {{plural_you:échenlo|echadlo}} al río Nilo. Pero a todas las niñas {{plural_you:déjenlas|dejadlas}} vivir».

fr.L: Et Pharaon ordonna à tout son peuple, disant : « Tout fils qui naîtra, dans le Fleuve vous le jetterez ; et toute fille, vous la laisserez vivre. »
fr.B: Alors Pharaon donna cet ordre à tout son peuple : « Tout garçon qui naîtra devra être jeté dans le Nil, mais toute fille aura la vie sauve. »
fr.R: Alors Pharaon a donné un ordre à tous les Égyptiens : « Quand un bébé hébreu naît, si c’est un garçon, jetez-le dans le Nil. Mais laissez vivre toutes les petites filles. »

sw.L: Naye Farao akawaamuru watu wake wote, akisema, "Kila mwana atakayezaliwa, mtamtupa Mtoni; na kila binti mtamwacha hai."
sw.B: Kisha Farao akatoa amri kwa watu wake wote: "Kila mtoto wa kiume atakayezaliwa ni lazima atupwe katika mto Naili, lakini kila mtoto wa kike aachwe hai."
sw.R: Kisha Farao akawapa Wamisri wote amri hii: "Mtoto wa kiume wa Kiebrania akizaliwa, mtupeni katika Mto Naili. Lakini waacheni watoto wote wa kike waishi."

decisions.choice: every son who is born: the Hebrew text does not add "to the Hebrews"
alternatives: every son born to the Hebrews
decisions.reason: The Samaritan Pentateuch, the Septuagint and the Aramaic Targums add "to the Hebrews". The shorter Hebrew text is followed here, but the context shows that the Hebrew boys are meant.

decisions.choice: the River: the Nile
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament "the River" in Egypt means the Nile. The river the king uses to kill will become the place where Moses is saved (2:3-10).

decisions.choice: all his people: the king's third plan involves every Egyptian
decisions.reason: First forced labor, then the midwives in secret, now an open order to the whole nation.

decisions.choice: a Hebrew baby boy
decisions.reason: Readable names the Hebrew boys, as the context requires (see m1).
